names: Maximum PV open circuit array voltage
Maximum PV array open circuit voltage
rules.basis: Each of these names the PV or solar input and calls the figure a maximum, an open-circuit voltage or both; a sheet that says 'maximum input voltage' alone is the maker's business.

names: Max. PV short-circuit current per MPPT
Max. PV short-circuit current input per MPPT
rules.basis: A short-circuit current limit on a unit with a PV input is the array's; the registry asks it only of charge controllers and inverters, and a figure printed per MPPT is per input, which is the key's own scope.
Each names the PV or solar input and calls the figure its maximum power; a figure printed per bank voltage carries the voltage in its name and is read with it.
The tracker's voltage range under its own name; the value is a range or it is refused.

The bank voltages a unit is made for, or a battery's own, under names that say battery, system or nominal DC input; 'nominal voltage' alone is left to the maker, since an inverter's sheet may mean its AC side.

The charge current a charger or controller delivers, under names that say charge or charging current and call it maximum or rated; on a battery the same words are the battery's own limit, read under its key.
A battery's charge current limit under the names its makers print; the registry asks it only of batteries.
A battery's continuous discharge limit; a peak figure carries the word peak and is read under the peak key with its duration.
The peak is a number only with the time it holds for, which the key needs; a figure that does not say it is a gap.

On a battery, capacity is in ampere-hours; a lead-acid pack's needs the discharge rate the key asks for, which the Rolls sheets print in the name, 'Capacity at 20 Hour Rate', and a lithium pack's stands without one. The registry asks it only of batteries, and a figure in watt-hours is a gap that says so.
The nominal energy of a pack in watt-hours or kilowatt-hours, as lithium makers state it.

An inverter's continuous, rated or nominal output power under the names its makers print, with the ambient temperature read off the name where the sheet states one; a figure in VA is a gap until an apparent-power key exists, and 'rated power' alone is left to the maker, since a generator's sheet prints it too.
A surge or peak figure is a number only with the time it holds for, which the key needs and is read off the name where the sheet states it; the rest are gaps that say so.

names: Zero load power in search mode
rules.basis: What the inverter draws with nothing connected; the search-mode figures carry their mode in the name, and a figure in amps or with a mode the sheet names some other way is the maker's to map.

The nominal AC output voltage, one or several; a tolerance printed with it is refused rather than halved, and the registry asks it only of inverters, so a converter's 'rated output voltage' is never read here.
Names that say apparent power outright; a continuous figure under a watt name that a sheet prints in VA reaches this key through that name's rule instead.

The Sol-Ark 5K sheet states its off-grid peak in VA for 100 ms and 10 s, the time in the name; an overload figure under a watt name that a sheet prints in VA reaches this key through that name's rule.
A generator sheet's running watts is the power it sustains, under whichever fuel the name states; a bare figure under the name is in the watts the name carries.
A generator sheet's running power is the power it sustains, in the unit it prints.
A generator sheet's starting watts is what it gives for the seconds a motor takes to start, under whichever fuel the name states; a bare figure under the name is in the watts the name carries.
A generator sheet's starting power is what it gives for the seconds a motor takes to start, in the unit it prints.

A pump sheet's shut-off head, or its maximum total head, is the height of water it lifts against with no flow; a bare 'Total head' can be an operating point and stays a maker's own. A value printed as feet with the metres beside it is read as feet.
A pump sheet's maximum working pressure is the most it works at continuously.
